subQuestions.questionText: Refer to the sketch on the pattern and shape of rural settlements. The settlement pattern at A is … (Refer to the sketch in the question paper showing settlements A–F with key indicating cultivated land, trees, farmsteads and roads.)
subQuestions.memoText: Answer: Dispersed (accept isolated) (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText: The settlement pattern at B is … (Refer to the sketch in the question paper.)
subQuestions.memoText: Answer: Nucleated (accept clustered) (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText: Settlement (A/B) is likely to generate more profit. (Refer to the sketch in the question paper.)
subQuestions.memoText:
Answer: A (1 mark)
The nucleated settlement at B generates more profit due to clustering, but per the memo the answer is A. [Memo confirms A]

subQuestions.questionText: The river caused the settlement at C to have a … shape. (Refer to the sketch in the question paper.)
subQuestions.memoText: Answer: Linear (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText: The shape of the settlement at F is … (Refer to the sketch in the question paper.)
subQuestions.memoText: Answer: T (T-shaped) (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText: D is located on high ground due to the threat of flooding and is called a … settlement. (Refer to the sketch in the question paper.)
subQuestions.memoText: Answer: dry point (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText: E is close to a supply of water and is referred to as a … settlement. (Refer to the sketch in the question paper.)
subQuestions.memoText: Answer: wet point (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText: A … is an area, where a group of people live, that has buildings, communication networks and functions.
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: C (settlement) (1 mark)
A settlement is the area where people live with buildings, communication networks and functions.

subQuestions.questionText: … is the process whereby an increasing percentage of people live in urban areas as compared to rural areas.
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: D (Urbanisation) (1 mark)
Urbanisation is the process of an increasing percentage of people living in urban areas relative to rural areas.

subQuestions.questionText: … is the formless growth of urban areas.
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: C (Urban sprawl) (1 mark)
Urban sprawl refers to the formless, uncontrolled outward expansion of urban areas.

subQuestions.questionText: The physical growth of an urban settlement is referred to as urban …
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: A (expansion) (1 mark)
Urban expansion refers to the physical/spatial growth of an urban settlement.

subQuestions.questionText: The increase in the number of people living in urban areas is known as ...
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: B (urban growth) (1 mark)
Urban growth refers to the increase in the number of people living in urban areas.

subQuestions.questionText: The largest increase in the level of urbanisation in South Africa is from … (Table provided: 2018 = 66.4%, 2019 = 66.9%, 2020 = 67.2%, 2021 = 67.9%, 2022 = 68.3%)
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: C (2020 to 2021) (1 mark)
The increase from 67.2% to 67.9% (0.7%) is the largest single-year jump in the table.

subQuestions.questionText: The … of urbanisation refers to the pace at which urbanisation takes place.
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: A (rate) (1 mark)
The rate of urbanisation refers to the speed/pace at which urbanisation occurs.

subQuestions.questionText: The advantages of counterurbanisation for urban areas are decreased … (i) pollution. (ii) land value. (iii) aesthetic appeal. (iv) traffic congestion.
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: C ((i) and (iv)) (1 mark)
Counterurbanisation reduces pollution and traffic congestion in urban areas as people move out to rural/peri-urban areas.

subQuestions.questionText: Refer to the graph and cartoon on rural-urban migration. The graph shows the predicted (expected) difference in the percentage increase of people that moved from rural to urban areas between 2000 and 2030 (Asia 37→50, Africa 37→54, Europe 73→80, S America 76→85, N America 79→84). Which continent is predicted (expected) to have the highest percentage of people that would move to urban areas between 2000 and 2030?
subQuestions.memoText:
Answer: Africa (1 mark)
[Accept S America]
Africa shows the largest predicted increase from 37% to 54% (17% increase).

subQuestions.questionText: Determine the predicted (expected) difference in the percentage of people (answer to QUESTION 1.3.1) that would have moved between 2000 and 2030.
subQuestions.memoText:
Answer: 17% (2 marks) [Accept 9% if S America was named in 1.3.1]
For Africa: 54% − 37% = 17%
For S America: 85% − 76% = 9%

subQuestions.questionText: Why will the rate of urbanisation of the continent (answer to QUESTION 1.3.1) be so high?
subQuestions.memoText:
[ANY ONE - Award 2 marks]
• Large rural populations gives rise to a higher rate of urbanisation (2)
• Push factors from rural areas (accept examples) (2)
• Pull factors towards urban areas (accept examples) (2)

subQuestions.questionText: Why does the pull factor, indicated in the cartoon (Better jobs in the city), often lead to disappointment?
subQuestions.memoText:
[ANY TWO - Award 2 marks each]
• There are not enough jobs available (2)
• They expected better jobs but did not get it (2)
• People do not have the skills/experience (2)
• They do not have the necessary documentation/qualifications (2)
• Lack of access to information on employment opportunities (2)
• They may be paid lower salaries than expected (2)
• Corruption and Nepotism (2)

subQuestions.questionText: Suggest strategies that could be implemented in rural areas to reduce the rate of urbanisation.
subQuestions.memoText:
[ANY THREE - Award 2 marks each]
• Encouraging decentralisation of businesses/industries (2)
• Create employment opportunities (2)
• Upskilling and training (2)
• Improve infrastructural development (accept examples) (2)
• Provision/Supply of basic services (accept examples) (2)
• Effective policing (2)
• Promoting rural areas through cultural/sporting events (accept examples) (2)
• Attract tourists (2)
• Improve recreational facilities (accept examples) (2)
• Create more tourism attractions (accept examples) (2)
• Speed up land reform (accept examples) (2)
• Financial assistance/subsidies/incentives/investment (2)

subQuestions.questionText: Refer to the sketch on the multiple-nuclei model showing land-use zones 1–9 (1. CBD, 2. Light industries, 3. Low-income residential, 4. Middle-income residential, 5. High-income residential, 6. Heavy industries, 7. Outlying business district, 8. Residential estate, 9. Industrial estate). State TWO characteristics of the multiple-nuclei model evident in the sketch.
subQuestions.memoText:
[ANY TWO - Award 1 mark each]
• There are focal points (nuclei) around which the urban settlement develops (1)
• Location of land-use (zones) are based on compatibility (1)
• All land-use (zones) are present (1)

subQuestions.questionText: Identify land-use zone 1. (Refer to the multiple-nuclei model sketch in the question paper.)
subQuestions.memoText: Answer: Central business district (CBD) (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText: Account for the location of land-use zone 1.
subQuestions.memoText: Answer: Land-use zone 1 (CBD) is located in an area of high accessibility (2 marks)

subQuestions.label: 1.4.4(a)
subQuestions.questionText: Explain how the development of the outlying business district (OBD), labelled 7, was influenced by: (a) Crime rate
subQuestions.memoText:
[ANY ONE - Award 2 marks]
• High crime in the CBD caused commercial activities to move to the Outlying Business District (2)
• Low crime rates in the OBD will be more attractive for development (2)
[For part marking: 1 mark each for 'high crime in CBD' or 'low crime rates in OBD']

subQuestions.label: 1.4.4(b)
subQuestions.questionText: Explain how the development of the outlying business district (OBD), labelled 7, was influenced by: (b) Traffic congestion
subQuestions.memoText:
[ANY ONE - Award 2 marks]
• Less traffic congestion in the OBD will increase convenience/accessibility (2)
• More traffic congestion in the CBD reduces convenience/accessibility (2)
[For part marking: 1 mark each for 'less traffic in OBD' or 'more traffic in CBD']

subQuestions.questionText: Why will the multiple-nuclei model depicted in the sketch not apply to all urban areas?
subQuestions.memoText:
[ANY THREE - Award 2 marks each]
• Urban areas have different nuclei (accept examples) (2)
• Level and rate of development differs (2)
• Different amounts of space available for the expansion of urban areas (2)
• Natural resources found in urban areas differ (accept examples) (2)
• Physical barriers (obstacles) that can prevent expansion (2)
• Different location of urban areas (2)
• Poor planning by municipalities (2)
• Restricted financial budgets (2)
• Historical/cultural factors have an impact (2)
• Transport infrastructure differs (2)

subQuestions.questionText: Refer to the photograph and extract on urban blight (urban decay) titled 'Reclaiming Transition Zone (Zone of Decay)' about Maboneng Precinct and Fordsburg gentrification. Define the concept urban blight.
subQuestions.memoText:
Answer: Deterioration of urban areas/buildings (2 marks)
[CONCEPT MARK]

subQuestions.questionText: Give evidence from the photograph that urban blight has taken place.
subQuestions.memoText:
[ANY ONE - Award 1 mark]
• Buildings are in a poor condition (accept examples) (1)
• Graffiti on the buildings (1)
• Litter/Pollution (in the area) (1)

subQuestions.questionText: Why is urban blight more dominant in the transition zone (zone of decay) than in other land-use zones?
subQuestions.memoText:
[ANY TWO - Award 2 marks each]
• Area of future expansion of the CBD/Zone of change/Invasion and succession (2)
• Attracts low income occupants/students (2)
• Landlords do not occupy/maintain/upgrade buildings (2)
• Buildings are left vacant (2)
• Buildings are illegally occupied (2)
• Lack of basic services (2)
• Overcrowding because of its proximity to the CBD (2)
• Immigrants are attracted due to the low cost of the dwellings (2)
• Social ills are prevalent (2)

subQuestions.questionText: In a paragraph of approximately EIGHT lines, explain the positive impact of gentrification on the transition zone (zone of decay).
subQuestions.memoText:
[ANY FOUR - Award 2 marks each]
• People will have better quality housing (2)
• People will have better access to basic services (2)
• Creates an improved aesthetic appeal (2)
• Reduces the crime rate in the area (2)
• Area becomes more attractive to tourists (2)
• It will attract more businesses (accept examples) (2)
• It will create more employment opportunities (2)
• Property values will increase (2)
• Rates collected can be used in the maintenance of the area (2)
• It will create a healthier environment (2)
• There will be improvements in infrastructure (2)
• Attracts more affluent people (2)
[Paragraph format expected]

subQuestions.questionText: … core industrial region contributes the lowest percentage to the GDP in South Africa. (Table provided: Durban-Pinetown 16.3%, South-western Cape 14.2%, Gauteng (PWV) 35.2%, Port Elizabeth-Uitenhage 7.9%)
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: B (Port Elizabeth-Uitenhage) (1 mark)
Port Elizabeth-Uitenhage contributes the lowest at 7.9% of GDP.

subQuestions.questionText: The … is the main source of water for the Gauteng (PWV) core industrial region.
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: C (Vaal Dam) (1 mark)
The Vaal Dam is the main source of water for the Gauteng (PWV) core industrial region.

subQuestions.questionText: Access to … is an advantage of the Port Elizabeth-Uitenhage core industrial region compared to the Gauteng (PWV) core industrial region.
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: D (harbours) (1 mark)
Port Elizabeth-Uitenhage has the advantage of harbour access being a coastal region, unlike inland Gauteng.

subQuestions.questionText: … is the main industry located in the Gauteng (PWV) core industrial region.
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: A (Iron and steel) (1 mark)
Iron and steel is the main industry in the Gauteng (PWV) region.

subQuestions.questionText: The Coega Industrial Development Zone is found in the … core industrial region.
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: B (Port Elizabeth-Uitenhage) (1 mark)
The Coega IDZ is located near Port Elizabeth (Gqeberha).

subQuestions.questionText: The main raw materials found in the Gauteng (PWV) core industrial region include … and … (i) gold (ii) fruit (iii) iron ore (iv) fish
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: B ((i) and (iii)) (1 mark)
Gold and iron ore are the main raw materials of Gauteng (PWV).

subQuestions.questionText: The dominant industrial activities in the Port Elizabeth-Uitenhage core industrial region are …
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: A (car assembly and textiles) (1 mark)
Port Elizabeth-Uitenhage is dominated by car assembly (e.g. VW, Ford) and textiles.

subQuestions.questionText: The disadvantages of industrial centralisation to the Gauteng (PWV) core industrial region are … (i) water shortages. (ii) a small labour force. (iii) small markets. (iv) air pollution.
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: C ((i) and (iv)) (1 mark)
Water shortages and air pollution are major disadvantages of industrial centralisation in Gauteng.

subQuestions.questionText: Choose an answer from COLUMN B that matches the statement in COLUMN A. Term used for unregistered businesses. (Y: formal sector / Z: informal sector)
subQuestions.memoText:
Answer: Z (informal sector) (1 mark)
The informal sector consists of unregistered businesses.

subQuestions.questionText: Characteristic of the informal sector. (Y: workers are self-employed / Z: workers are employed by a national enterprise (business))
subQuestions.memoText:
Answer: Y (workers are self-employed) (1 mark)
In the informal sector, workers are typically self-employed.

subQuestions.questionText: Reason for a high number of immigrants entering the informal sector. (Y: lack of documentation / Z: availability of jobs)
subQuestions.memoText:
Answer: Y (lack of documentation) (1 mark)
Immigrants often lack documentation required for the formal sector.

subQuestions.questionText: Example of an informal sector. (Y: PEP stores / Z: car guard)
subQuestions.memoText:
Answer: Z (car guard) (1 mark)
A car guard is an example of informal sector employment.

subQuestions.questionText: Benefit for consumers buying goods from an informal trader. (Y: quality products at a higher price / Z: goods can be purchased at a lower price)
subQuestions.memoText:
Answer: Z (goods can be purchased at a lower price) (1 mark)
Informal traders typically offer goods at lower prices.

subQuestions.questionText: Reason for the growth of the informal sector in South Africa. (Y: limited jobs available in the formal sector / Z: jobs available in the formal sector)
subQuestions.memoText:
Answer: Y (limited jobs available in the formal sector) (1 mark)
Limited formal sector employment forces people into the informal sector.

subQuestions.questionText: Challenge facing the informal sector. (Y: provision of low interest loans / Z: exposed to harsh weather conditions)
subQuestions.memoText:
Answer: Z (exposed to harsh weather conditions) (1 mark)
Informal traders frequently work outdoors and face exposure to harsh weather.

subQuestions.questionText: Refer to the graph and extract on food insecurity. (Graph shows global food insecurity rising from 198 million in 2019 to +828 million in 2023). State the trend evident on the graph with regard to global food insecurity from 2019 to 2023.
subQuestions.memoText: Answer: Upward trend/increasing/positive trend (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText: According to the extract, what are the reasons for the trend shown on the graph?
subQuestions.memoText:
[ANY TWO - Award 1 mark each]
• Climate change (1)
• COVID pandemic (1)
• Poverty (1)
• Wars/conflict (1)
• Global food trade restrictions (1)
• Reducing SA's imports (1)
• Food export bans (1)
• Increase in food prices/higher inflation rates (1)

subQuestions.questionText: What positive impact could the global food trade restriction measures have on South Africa?
subQuestions.memoText:
[ANY ONE - Award 2 marks]
• It forces us to produce our own food (2)
• Leads to economic growth (accept examples) (2)
• More jobs are created (2)
• This will upskill people (2)
• Food prices will eventually drop (2)
• Lower inflation rates (2)

subQuestions.questionText: Explain how TWO physical factors negatively impact South Africa's food production.
subQuestions.memoText:
[ANY TWO - Award 2 marks each]
• Harsh climatic/weather conditions (climate change, droughts, thunderstorms, floods and frost) destroy crops (2)
• Lower than average rainfall reduces harvests (2)
• Pests and diseases damage crops (2)
• Soil erosion/Poor soil quality decreases the amount of land available for the cultivation of crops (2)
• Desertification reduces the amount of available fertile land (2)
[For part marking: 1 mark each for naming the factor; maximum of 2 marks]

subQuestions.questionText: Suggest measures that government can implement (put in place) to support farmers in achieving food security in South Africa.
subQuestions.memoText:
[ANY THREE - Award 2 marks each]
• Facilitate training/upskilling of farmers (2)
• Encourage research/scientific farming methods (accept examples) (2)
• Easier access to funding/economic support (accept examples) (2)
• Accelerate land reform (2)
• Support small-scale/large-scale farmers (accept examples) (2)
• Shift from subsistence to commercial farming (2)
• Infrastructure to support agriculture (accept examples) (2)
• Improve farm security (2)
• More efficient food storage (accept examples) (2)
• Promote agricultural processing industries (2)

subQuestions.questionText: Refer to the infographic on platinum mining (showing PGM production, location map of platinum mines in Limpopo, North West, Mpumalanga, Free State, and the platinum supply graph from 2016-2023). What percentage of the world's platinum reserves does South Africa have?
subQuestions.memoText: Answer: (Over) 80% (1 mark)

subQuestions.label: 2.4.2(a)
subQuestions.questionText: Give evidence from the extract that platinum production in South Africa is influenced (affected) by a: (a) Social factor
subQuestions.memoText: Answer: Labour strikes (1 mark)

subQuestions.label: 2.4.2(b)
subQuestions.questionText: Give evidence from the extract that platinum production in South Africa is influenced (affected) by a: (b) Service delivery factor
subQuestions.memoText:
[ANY ONE - Award 1 mark]
• Access to affordable and reliable electricity (1)
• Water distribution infrastructure (1)
• Water security (1)

subQuestions.questionText: Refer to the map and name TWO provinces where platinum is mined.
subQuestions.memoText:
[ANY TWO - Award 1 mark each]
• North West (1)
• Mpumalanga (1)
• Limpopo (1)
• Free State (1)
• Gauteng (1)

subQuestions.questionText: Describe the general trend of the platinum supply between 2016 and 2018 and between 2020 to 2023, by referring to the graph.
subQuestions.memoText:
Award 1 mark each:
• 2016 – 2018: upward trend/increased (1)
• 2020 – 2023: downward trend/decreased (1)

subQuestions.questionText: In a paragraph of approximately EIGHT lines, suggest strategies that government can implement (put in place) to address challenges of platinum production.
subQuestions.memoText:
[ANY FOUR - Award 2 marks each]
• Creating partnerships/relationships (with communities/mine unions) regarding labour strikes (accept examples) (2)
• Use renewable sources of energy (accept examples) (2)
• Provision of greater access to basic services (accept examples) (2)
• Research relating to platinum mining (accept examples) (2)
• Reduce investors' fears of nationalisation/political instability (2)
• Ensure occupational safety of miners (2)
• Educate miners on HIV/AIDS (2)
• Improve infrastructure (accept examples) (2)
• Engage in profit sharing with mine workers (2)
• Sustainable minimum wage (2)
• More advanced technology in mines (2)
• Upskilling of mineworkers (2)
[Paragraph format expected]

subQuestions.questionText: Refer to the extract on the Wild Coast Spatial Development Initiative (SDI) and the N2 Wild Coast Toll Road Project. State ONE key objective of Spatial Development Initiatives (SDI) in South Africa.
subQuestions.memoText:
[ANY ONE - Award 1 mark]
• Sustainable economic growth (1)
• Create employment (1)
• To encourage investment (1)
• Develop physical infrastructure (1)
• Sustainable development in underdeveloped areas (1)

subQuestions.questionText: In which province is the Wild Coast Spatial Development Initiative (SDI) located?
subQuestions.memoText: Answer: Eastern Cape (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText: According to the extract, by how much will the income of the local industries increase?
subQuestions.memoText: Answer: R360,4 million (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText: State TWO physical factors that would encourage tourism in the Wild Coast Spatial Development Initiative (SDI).
subQuestions.memoText:
[ANY TWO - Award 1 mark each]
• Coastline (1)
• Beaches (1)
• Warm oceans (1)
• Landforms (1)
• Scenic beauty (1)
• Large diversity of indigenous fauna/flora (1)

subQuestions.questionText: How would the N2 Wild Coast toll road project encourage economic development of the Wild Coast Spatial Development Initiative (SDI)?
subQuestions.memoText:
[ANY TWO - Award 2 marks each]
• It would create more employment (2)
• The area would be more accessible to tourists (2)
• It would stimulate more economic investment (2)
• Goods would be able to be transported to and from the area (2)
• Bulk transport would be possible (2)
• There would be more opportunities for entrepreneurship (2)
• More jobs will create a larger market for goods (2)
• It will create a multiplier effect (2)
• There will be upskilling of the labour force (2)

subQuestions.questionText: Explain why the Wild Coast Spatial Development Initiative (SDI) has experienced challenges with regard to achieving its key objectives (goals).
subQuestions.memoText:
[ANY THREE - Award 2 marks each]
• Traditional and cultural beliefs have restricted the use of certain land (2)
• A skills shortage in the secondary and tertiary sector will limit sustainable development (2)
• High crime levels due to poverty in the area discourage investment (2)
• The community has rejected the option of extracting gas from the ocean that would have provided employment/boosted the economy (2)
• Illegal mining of building sand that has destroyed natural vegetation/forests decreasing tourism (2)
• Municipal land is illegally sold off below land value that depletes municipal coffers (2)
• Locals challenged the building of the toll road delaying its completion (2)
• To protect cultural values and interests, local communities are reluctant to promote tourism (2)
[For part marking: 1 mark each for naming the challenge; maximum of 3 marks]
